claims.claim: 1 year used industrial machine working perfectly
claims.evidence: Photos show an industrial sewing machine, but there is no proof of age (purchase date) and no demonstration/testing to confirm it is working perfectly.

risks.risk: Exact model/variant is not readable, so the correct parts, service history, and comparable pricing are uncertain.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the machine’s model/serial plate (or the label that includes the full model code) plus the underside/side nameplate if present.
risks.if_unproven: Price as a generic Emel industrial sewing machine with unknown model, and assume typical used-condition risk (not “perfectly working”).

risks.risk: “Working perfectly” is not proven; sewing machines can have issues (timing, motor speed control, feed mechanism, needle bar timing, thread tension).
risks.proof: A short video of the machine running and stitching a sample fabric (showing feed, tension, and consistent stitch formation) with sound.
risks.if_unproven: Price as not guaranteed/needs servicing (worst case: treat as not confirmed working).

risks.risk: Missing/incorrect accessories (presser feet, bobbins, needles, clutch/motor parts) can affect usability and cost to get it running.
risks.proof: A photo list of included accessories: needles, bobbins, presser feet, power cable, foot pedal, and any manuals/parts.
risks.if_unproven: Price assuming minimal included items and possible need to buy missing accessories.

risks.risk: Electrical and control issues (power supply, foot pedal, speed controller) may not show in still photos.
risks.proof: A photo/video showing the machine powered on, speed control working, and foot pedal response.
risks.if_unproven: Price as requiring electrical check/possible repair.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the full model/serial plate (clear enough to read all characters).
Video: power on + foot pedal test + stitching a short sample (show stitch quality).
Photos of included accessories (needles, bobbins, presser feet, pedal, power cable) laid out.
response.reason: The photos identify it as an Emel industrial sewing machine, but the exact model number and any proof of “working perfectly” are not visible. Without a readable model plate and a stitching test, a reliable worst-case price can’t be set confidently.
